name: Variational Optimization with Locally Orderless Images (LOI)
definition: A method for differentiable rendering optimization that combines variational derivatives with local histogram matching to recover parameters (e.g., kaleidoscope configuration, particle positions, glass orb position) from images where RGB gradients are unstable or insufficient due to high variance or local minima.
summary: LOI is a differentiable rendering technique that recovers scene parameters by matching local intensity histograms, avoiding the alignment sensitivity and instability of standard RGB gradient methods.
